name_note: GTDB labels this species Blautia_A luti_A, a genome-based split of the classical Blautia luti.

sentences.text: Blautia luti is described as a gut acetogen, and a study identified acetate, succinate, lactate, formate and hydrogen as end products of its sugar fermentation.
It notes that species of the genus Blautia are commonly found in the human gut, while little is known about their physiology and specific role there.
In a rat model, a study gave Blautia luti as a daily probiotic and reported reduced grade 3 diarrhoea in one schedule group compared with neratinib alone.
The complete genome of the type strain JCM 17040 is a circular chromosome of 3,741,599 base pairs with a G+C content of 42.9 percent.
